_comment: Enforcement-boundary labels are not always Lean definition names. This maps a label to the definition the arm reaches, so scripts/check_live_arm_per_core_routing.py can walk it. Missing alias = hard failure, never a silent skip. Every entry here is VERIFIED against the live dispatch arm in SeLe4n/Kernel/API.lean (PR #861 review round 15): the gate rejects an alias the arm does not call, so a coincidental name match can no longer stand in for the real operation. Round 16: the verification now strips leading-dot constructor references before looking for the root, so an arm header (`| .schedContextUnbind =>`) or a decode guard (`decoded.syscallId = .schedContextUnbind`) can no longer stand in for a call — which is what let the schedContextUnbind label pass while the arm called the OnCore wrapper.
_alt_note: Round 20: a `<label>#alt` entry names the OTHER production root of a syscall that has two dispatch arms — the unchecked arm alongside the information-flow-checked one.  Both are walked.  Before this the arms were concatenated and only the mapped root was scanned, so a boot-pinned regression confined to the unchecked arm left the gate green.
_reply_seam_note: Fault handling (v0.34.44): both `.reply` arms now dispatch through the reply seam `replyTransferOnCore` / `replyTransferOnCoreChecked` — seL4's `doReplyTransfer`, which branches on the answered thread's `pendingFault` before transferring anything. A fault handler holds nothing but the reply capability the fault Call gave it, so without that branch the reply-based restart is verified and unreachable. The seam is the root the walk starts from; the cross-core reply chain it calls on the ordinary branch is reached transitively, and the fault reply on the other branch is now audited too. The reach depth went 2 -> 3 in the same cut, because this extra hop would otherwise have shortened the walk into the reply chain by one level.
_inert_note: A `<label>#inert` entry declares that one of this syscall's dispatch arms performs NO operation, so there is no body to walk for boot-pinned scheduler reads.  Declared rather than inferred, and VERIFIED by the gate (the arm must call nothing and must produce an error), so an edit that gives the arm a call turns the exemption back into a demand for a root.  The capability dispatcher's `.yield` arm is the one such arm (see `_yield_note`).
_audit_reader_note: PR #870 review: the enforcement-boundary label for the audit-trail read is now `auditReadFromCore` — the LIVE entry point the `.auditRead` arm calls — so no alias is needed and the routing walk audits the subject-resolution seam itself (the first cut labelled the inner query `auditReadWord`, which takes a caller-supplied reader domain; coverage tracking that helper would have stayed green had the live seam drifted onto the confused-clearance shape).  The drain's label was the live entry from the start.
_yield_note: The yield syscall invokes no capability: the dispatcher runs it from a guard ahead of the caller's CSpace lookup, and that guard arm calls `dispatchYield`, the `Kernel` wrapper over `yieldOnCore`, so the walk starts there.  The capability dispatcher's own `.yield` arm is an unreachable refusal spelled for exhaustiveness (`fun _ => .error .illegalState`) and is inert.
